items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had also engaged Arstella Whittier as vocalist... We had been together in the Philippines.

ctx.x: of Willie "the Lion" Smith and he did a good imitation of singing like Fats.

George Smith was an up to date drummer who could not have been in France more than a couple of years before I arrived in 48. He liked to do singing imitations of Louis Armstrong which didn't sound very good to me. "Big Boy" Goudie had a very personal style on tenor and played very good New Orleans style clarinet. "Bass" Hill was always known as a solid bass man and had played with many of the big named bands in New York. We had been together in the Philippines. The weakest man in the band was Fred Palmer who had…

Other than the fact that we had no music on the stands, we still made a hit with the public at the Chikito. Later Norman Lester wrote some original tunes which actually had no swing possibilities and although he was a good piano man, he was not an arranger. But we played the tunes every night because I was a begger and had no choice.
